stem: Which mechanism best explains methotrexate's antineoplastic effect?

options.A: Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase, reducing tetrahydrofolate-dependent purine and thymidylate synthesis and interfering with DNA synthesis and replication.
options.B: Induction of DNA strand breaks through interaction with DNA topoisomerase II, producing cell-cycle arrest and cell death.
options.C: Formation of interstrand and intrastrand DNA cross-links that interfere with normal transcription and DNA replication.
options.D: Stabilization of microtubules by preventing depolymerization, disrupting the dynamic microtubule changes required for mitosis.

rationale: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, preventing normal tetrahydrofolate-dependent synthesis of purine nucleotides and thymidylate and thereby interfering with DNA synthesis, repair, and cellular replication. A is therefore correct. B describes the topoisomerase-II-associated DNA strand-break mechanism of etoposide, C describes cisplatin DNA cross-linking, and D describes paclitaxel-mediated microtubule stabilization. These are plausible antineoplastic mechanisms but are not methotrexate's mechanism.
educational_objective: Identify methotrexate as a folate analog metabolic inhibitor whose antineoplastic action includes inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase and interference with purine, thymidylate, and DNA synthesis.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_locator: Full Prescribing Information §12.1 Mechanism of Action
source_claim_supported: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolic acid reductase; reduced tetrahydrofolates are required for purine nucleotide and thymidylate synthesis, so methotrexate interferes with DNA synthesis, repair, and cellular replication.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: Review pertinent medication data; Educate client about medications; Handle and administer high-risk medications safely

correction_summary: Removed the unsupported 'higher-dose cancer therapy' qualifier, corrected the source identity from tablets to the exact Methotrexate Injection label at the supplied set-id, and replaced implausible non-oncology distractors with verified alternative antineoplastic mechanisms (etoposide topoisomerase-II DNA strand breaks, cisplatin DNA cross-links, and paclitaxel microtubule stabilization). Reduced difficulty from hard to moderate.
